title: ask-weave-collector-aug-2026
content:
Purpose and framing:
- Quick synthesis notebook compiling recent customer asks from May-July 2026.
- Goal: produce a compact set of prioritized action candidates (quick fixes, experiments, product bets) for Q3 planning and handoff to product + eng.
- Not exhaustive; this is an "ask-weave" — stitch together small signals into coherent micro-themes.

Methodology / sources: 
- Inputs: support tickets (sampled), CS field interviews (8 customers), NPS follow-ups, product analytics (token latency histograms), and recent sales engineering notes.
- Prominent threads surfaced via fast clustering (internal script) then hand-validated by CS leads (Maya).
- Linked artifacts (above) include the canonical Confluence capture and several Jira refs.

Top micro-themes (high signal):
1) Predictable tail latency pain (20% of vignettes)
   - Customers report occasional 300–800ms tail spikes on streaming endpoints even when median is ~60ms.
   - Quote: "Most requests are fine, but spikes break our UX flows and we lose conversations." — Fintech customer
   - Common ask: better visibility (per-request latency drilldown) and automatic fallback configuration.

2) Embeddings stability and re-indexing ergonomics (18% of vignettes)
   - Customers want deterministic-ish embeddings across minor model upgrades and clear re-index guidance.
   - Ask: migration tools / diff tooling for embedding drift and simple re-index dashboards.

3) Error transparency & retry guidance (15%)
   - Confusion around 5xx vs model-timeout vs infra-throttles. Asks for clearer error codes and recommended retry/backoff policies.

4) Cost-control primitives around batching and caching (14%)
   - Customers ask for a UI to preview cost delta for changing batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles.

5) Function-calling / tooling edgecases (12%)
   - Several customers hit schema-mismatch failures and want better example scaffolds + sandboxed simulations to validate tool outputs.

Representative vignettes (one-line):
- SaaS analytics startup: "We saw a backlog build on weekdays — need autoscale buffer for bursts without doubling cost." (ticket CS-412)
- E-commerce vendor: "Embeddings drifted after a patch; we had to re-run the reindex — no diff made it hard to triage."
- Healthcare POC: "500s look like model errors but they were cert/timeouts — we almost lost pilot sign-off."

Priority asks (suggested ranking + rationale):
A. Quick wins (<= 2 engineer-weeks):
   1) Add per-request latency taggable drilldown in Console (UI + trace link) — low effort, high impact on trust. Owner: Liam.
   2) Surface richer error taxonomy in responses + expand SDK error classes with recommended retry semantics. (CS + SDK). Owner: Priya.
   3) Small UX flows: add a "reindex preview" that shows sample diffs for embeddings (first-pass: 50 docs). Owner: Product-optimize PM.

B. Medium bets (2–8 engineer-weeks):
   1) Embeddings migration helper: diff tooling + optional idempotent reindex pipeline (configurable batch windows, checkpointing). Rationale: reduces customer churn risk on model upgrades.
   2) Cost preview simulator: Console tool to model cost change when toggling batching/caching/quantization for a given request histogram. Rationale: empowers customers to self-serve cost tuning.

C. Strategic product bets (quarter+):
   1) Smart fallback policies: policy DSL to route to cheaper/compatible model variants automatically when latency SLOs are at risk. Requires integration with routing and rollout systems.
   2) Sandboxed tool-calling playground: deterministic validation harness for schema/contract conformance across tool chains.

Risk flags & constraints: 
- Observability gaps: We currently lack easy joins between per-request telemetry and customer-visible Console traces — this increases triage time. (See INFRA-998).
- Data-sensitivity: healthcare customers require audit logs for reindex operations; must design with Private deployment needs in mind.

Quant metrics to track (proposed):
- # of customer incidents attributed to tail latency per month
- Average time-to-resolution for embedding drift incidents
- Adoption % for Console "cost preview" once shipped (target 30% of active teams in 90 days)
- Reduction in CS triage time for error-coded incidents

Suggested owners & ask for meetings: 
- Quick-wins triage sync (30 min): Evan + Liam + PRD lead + Maya (this week).
- Embedding helper scoping: Product-optimize + Applied ML + Solutions Eng (1.5 hr scoping).

Actionable next steps (concrete):
1) Evan to open feature-brief PRD stub in Confluence with acceptance criteria for Quick wins by 2026-08-06.
2) Liam to prototype Console latency drilldown design + API contract (demo in 2 weeks).
3) Priya to draft SDK error class spec and sample retry recipes; present to SDK team.
4) CS to collect 10 anonymized reindex logs from customers for migration helper design (Maya).

Unresolved questions / notes-to-self:
- How tightly coupled should embedding diffs be to model versioning? (tradeoffs for storage & compute).
- For cost simulator, do we model token-level latency distributions per-model or per-route? (need product decision)
- Confirm compliance requirements for reindex audit trail across Private deployments.

Appendix: small backlog of related tickets (for easy cross-ref):
- CS-412: weekday backlog / autoscale buffer
- CS-427: embedding drift complaint (customer X)
- INFRA-998: telemetry join gaps for per-request tracing
- OPT-221: cost-preview spike analysis (prototype notebook)

Closing note: this is intentionally pragmatic and collage-like — action is more valuable than perfect taxonomy. The ask-weave approach surfaces small, high-impact fixes we can deliver quickly and larger bets we should scope. Happy to prune/expand based on engineering capacity.

-- Evan
